recognize_zh: 單一受感染紅血球內含形狀不規則的阿米巴樣滋養體（amoeboid trophozoite）與金褐色瘧色素，細胞質布滿細小粉紅色 Schüffner 小點（Schüffner dots），符合間日瘧原蟲（P. vivax）。
features: Single parasitized red cell, about the size of or slightly larger than neighboring RBCs
Fine, evenly distributed pink-red stippling (Schüffner dots) throughout the host cell
Irregular amoeboid trophozoite/early schizont with several chromatin dots and golden-brown hemozoin pigment
Uninfected RBCs normocytic and normochromic; no multiply infected cells or banana-shaped gametocytes
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood smear shows normocytic, normochromic red cells with a single parasitized erythrocyte. The infected cell is not smaller than surrounding RBCs and contains an irregular, amoeboid late trophozoite/early schizont with several chromatin masses and golden-brown pigment, while its cytoplasm is filled with fine pink Schüffner stippling. No multiply infected erythrocytes, appliqué forms or crescentic gametocytes are seen. Findings are consistent with Plasmodium vivax infection; parasitemia should be quantified on thin film.

ddx.vs: P. ovale also shows Schüffner-type (James) dots but the infected RBC is oval with fimbriated edges and the trophozoite is compact rather than amoeboid.
P. falciparum shows delicate ring forms with double chromatin dots, frequent multiply infected RBCs, crescentic gametocytes and Maurer clefts, without enlargement or Schüffner dots.
P. malariae infects small RBCs lacking stippling and forms band trophozoites and rosette schizonts with coarse dark pigment.
Babesia forms small pleomorphic rings or Maltese-cross tetrads without hemozoin pigment or Schüffner dots.
